hooks.text: This nebula casts visible shadows at night.
Four hundred fifty thousand suns pack this single star nursery.
A monstrous star factory in space creates the most massive stars known.

title: The Nebula Bright Enough to Cast Shadows
description: Discover the Tarantula Nebula, a star nursery so intensely luminous it would cast visible shadows at night if it were as close as Orion.

beats.text: This nebula casts visible shadows at night.
beats.visual: James Webb Space Telescope NIRCam image of the Tarantula Nebula, 2022
queries: James Webb Space Telescope Tarantula Nebula NIRCam

beats.text: Located in a neighboring galaxy, it is extremely vast.
beats.visual: Wide-field view of the Large Magellanic Cloud galaxy, 2010

beats.text: Astronomers measure its span at roughly one thousand light-years.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope mosaic of the Tarantula Nebula, 2018

beats.text: Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille discovered the star nursery back in 1751.
beats.visual: Portrait of astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille, 1750

beats.text: Its dense core packs four hundred fifty thousand suns of mass.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope view of the R136 star cluster, 2020

beats.text: It houses the most massive stars ever discovered by science.
beats.visual: Hubble close-up of massive stars in the Tarantula Nebula, 2015

beats.text: No ordinary night sky compares to where this glowing cosmic beast casts visible shadows.
beats.visual: James Webb Space Telescope MIRI view of the Tarantula Nebula, 2022
queries: James Webb Space Telescope Tarantula Nebula MIRI
